prompt: Which sentence would best introduce the paragraph?
passage: (1) First, each student wrote a letter describing a normal school day in 2026. (2) Then the class added a newspaper, a class photo and a list of the most popular songs. (3) Mr. Brooks sealed everything inside a metal box and buried it beside the flagpole. (4) The box will not be opened until the year 2046.
choices: Mr. Brooks's class wrote letters to pen pals at a school in another country.
Mr. Brooks's class made a time capsule for students twenty years from now.
Time capsules have been buried under buildings and statues for hundreds of years.
Mr. Brooks's class found an old metal box buried beside the school flagpole.
why_wrong: builds an introduction from the word "letter", but the letters describe a school day and go into a box, not to pen pals
introduces time capsules in general, not what this class did
reverses the story: the class buried the box rather than finding one
explanation: The paragraph tells how one class filled and buried a box to be opened in 2046, which is a time capsule for future students. The other sentences introduce pen pals, the history of time capsules, or a box that was found.

prompt: Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
passage: (1) Ana wanted to grow sunflowers taller than her house. (2) In April, she planted twelve seeds along the fence and watered them every evening. (3) When a storm knocked over half the plants in June, she tied the rest to wooden stakes. (4) By August, four sunflowers stood higher than the roof of her house.
choices: Ana decided that sunflowers were too much work and planted beans instead.
Sunflowers can grow more than ten feet tall in a single summer.
Ana's sunflowers were the tallest flowers in the whole state.
Ana's patience and care had paid off, even after the storm.
why_wrong: contradicts the paragraph, which ends with Ana reaching her goal
turns from Ana's story to a general fact about sunflowers
claims something the paragraph gives no evidence for
explanation: The paragraph shows Ana working toward a goal, overcoming the storm, and reaching it. A conclusion should sum that up, as the sentence about patience and care does. The others contradict the ending, drift to a general fact, or make an unsupported claim.

prompt: Which sentence, if added after sentence 3, would best support the writer's claim?
passage: (1) Our class should take its spring field trip to the science museum instead of the zoo. (2) We are studying electricity and magnets this spring. (3) The museum's energy hall lets students build circuits and test magnets with their own hands. (4) A trip to the museum would help us understand what we are learning in class.
choices: Last year's class also visited the science museum and liked the gift shop best.
The museum also offers a free workshop for school groups on how electric motors work.
The zoo has a new baby giraffe that many students in our class want to see.
The science museum is about the same distance from our school as the zoo.
why_wrong: gives a reason that has nothing to do with learning, the writer's point
gives a reason to choose the zoo, which works against the claim
states a fact that favors neither place
explanation: The writer argues for the museum because it fits what the class is studying. A free workshop on electric motors adds another link to the electricity unit. The other sentences praise the gift shop, favor the zoo, or are neutral.

prompt: Which sentence would best introduce the paragraph?
passage: (1) Each spring, the students choose a theme by voting in their homerooms. (2) Then local artists help them turn their sketches into one large design. (3) Over three weekends, students and parents paint the design on the wall behind the gym. (4) This year's mural, which shows the town's river and its wildlife, took more than two hundred gallons of paint.
choices: At Lakeview Middle School, students study the history of painting and famous murals in art class.
At Lakeview Middle School, a professional artist paints a new mural on the gym each year.
At Lakeview Middle School, painting a new mural each year is a project the whole school shares.
At Lakeview Middle School, the river behind the gym is home to herons, turtles and a family of beavers.
why_wrong: introduces art history lessons, which the paragraph never mentions
says an artist paints the mural, but students and parents do the painting
introduces one detail of this year's mural instead of the whole project
explanation: The paragraph describes how students, artists and parents make a mural together every year. The sentence about a shared yearly project names that subject. The others introduce a different topic, contradict who paints, or focus on one detail.

prompt: Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
passage: (1) Our school should start each day fifteen minutes later. (2) Doctors say that most students our age need about nine hours of sleep a night, but many get only seven. (3) Tired students have trouble paying attention in their first classes. (4) When a nearby district moved its start time later, attendance in first period rose.
choices: Starting school later would also give the buses more time to finish their morning routes across town.
Some students, however, like to arrive early so they can eat breakfast at school.
Most students our age need about nine hours of sleep a night.
Starting school a little later would help students come to class rested and ready to learn.
why_wrong: adds a new reason about buses at the very end instead of closing the argument about sleep
ends with a point against the writer's claim
repeats one detail from sentence 2 instead of bringing the argument together
explanation: The paragraph argues that a later start would help tired students learn. A conclusion should tie the reasons together, as the sentence about coming to class rested does. The others add a new topic, weaken the claim, or repeat one detail.

prompt: Which sentence would best introduce the paragraph?
passage: (1) In the 1800s, keepers lived in small houses at the base of each tower. (2) Every evening at sunset, they climbed the stairs to light the lamp, and they trimmed its wick through the night. (3) During storms, they sometimes rowed out to rescue sailors whose ships had struck rocks. (4) Today, nearly all lighthouses run automatically, and many keepers' houses have become museums.
choices: Lighthouses were often painted with bold stripes or checks so that sailors could recognize them during the day.
Before lighthouses were automated, keepers had little to do except watch the sea.
Before lighthouses were automated, keeping one burning was demanding and sometimes dangerous work.
Many old lighthouse keepers' houses along the coast have been turned into museums for visitors.
why_wrong: introduces how lighthouses look, which the paragraph never discusses
contradicts the nightly duties and storm rescues the paragraph describes
introduces one detail from the last sentence instead of the paragraph's subject
explanation: Sentences 1-3 describe the hard, risky work of lighthouse keepers, and sentence 4 explains that it has ended. The sentence about demanding and dangerous work introduces that. The others discuss paint, deny the work, or focus on museums.

prompt: Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
passage: (1) When Owen joined the debate team, he was so nervous that his hands shook during practice. (2) His coach told him to rehearse each speech out loud in front of a mirror every night. (3) At his first tournament, he lost both rounds but wrote down every question the judges asked. (4) By the spring tournament, Owen answered questions calmly and won three of his four rounds.
choices: Owen decided that debate was not for him and joined the chess club.
Owen's coach had been on the debate team when she was in college.
Owen's steady practice had turned his nerves into confidence.
Owen hoped his school would host the spring tournament next year.
why_wrong: contradicts the paragraph, which ends with Owen succeeding
turns to a detail about the coach that the paragraph does not build toward
turns to a new wish instead of closing the story of Owen's growth
explanation: The paragraph traces how practice helped Owen go from shaking hands to calm answers and wins. The sentence about practice turning nerves into confidence sums that up. The others contradict the ending or turn to unrelated details.

prompt: Which sentence, if added after sentence 2, would best support the writer's claim?
passage: (1) Our town should build a skate park. (2) Right now, skaters use the library steps and the bank parking lot, where they get in the way of cars and people walking. (3) A park on the empty lot behind the pool would solve this problem.
choices: Skateboarding became an Olympic sport for the first time in 2021.
Many skaters in town are teenagers who also play other sports.
Some people in town think skateboarding is too dangerous for children and should not be encouraged.
A skate park would give skaters a safe place built for skating, away from traffic.
why_wrong: gives a true fact about skateboarding that says nothing about why this town needs a park
gives a detail about the skaters that does not support building a park
raises a concern against skateboarding, which weakens the claim
explanation: Sentence 2 describes a problem, and the claim is that a skate park would fix it. A safe place away from traffic answers that problem directly. The other sentences are unrelated or work against the claim.

prompt: Which sentence would best introduce the paragraph?
passage: (1) Engineers placed thousands of sensors along the bridge's cables and deck. (2) The sensors measure how much the bridge sways in the wind and how it reacts to heavy traffic. (3) If a reading falls outside its normal range, the system alerts an inspector within seconds. (4) Since the system was installed, inspectors have found two worn cables months before a routine check would have noticed them.
choices: The Harbor Bridge now watches its own health with a network of electronic sensors.
The Harbor Bridge is one of the longest bridges in the region and carries thousands of cars a day.
The Harbor Bridge was closed for two years while workers replaced every one of its cables.
Wind can cause long bridges to sway several feet back and forth during a strong storm.
why_wrong: introduces the bridge's size and traffic, which the paragraph does not discuss
introduces a repair project the paragraph never describes; it mentions only two worn cables
introduces a general fact about wind instead of the sensor system
explanation: The paragraph explains how sensors on the bridge detect problems and alert inspectors. The sentence about the bridge watching its own health with sensors introduces that topic. The others introduce size, a different repair, or a general fact.

prompt: Which sentence would best conclude the paragraph?
passage: (1) Our city should replace its old streetlights with LED bulbs. (2) LED lights use about half as much electricity as the bulbs we have now. (3) They also last several times longer, so workers would replace them far less often. (4) Because LEDs aim light downward, they would also cut the glow that hides the stars over our town.
choices: Switching to LEDs would make our streets as bright at night as they are during the day.
LED stands for light-emitting diode, a type of light first made in the 1960s.
Switching to LEDs would save money and energy while giving us clearer night skies.
Some residents prefer the warm color of the old streetlights to the light of LEDs.
why_wrong: overstates the brightness and clashes with the point about less glow
ends with a background fact instead of closing the argument
ends with a point against the writer's claim
explanation: The paragraph gives three reasons for LEDs: less electricity, longer life, and darker skies. The conclusion that brings those reasons together is the one about saving money and energy with clearer skies. The others overstate, drift to background, or weaken the claim.
